newsitem.title: USA: Interim police chief named in Los Angeles.
newsitem.headline: Interim police chief named in Los Angeles.

text.p: An interim chief was named Wednesday to head the police force in America's second largest city while the search for a new top cop continues.
The city's Police Commission chose current assistant chief Bayan Lewis to take over the Los Angeles Police Department after Willie Williams steps down May 18.
Commission president Ray Fisher said the panel voted 3-2 to name an interim chief who is not a candidate for the permanent job.
Williams, the city's first black police chief, was brought in to run the LAPD in 1992 in an effort to improve the department's battered image and poor morale.

His five-year contract expires in July and the city voted this moth not to renew it. Williams, who had threatened to sue the city if it was not renewed, opted instead to accept a $375,000 severance package.
Lewis currently heads the LAPD's Office of Operations, which oversees some 85 percent of the department's resources, including all patrol-related functions and most detective functions.
